chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man married a woman for one hundred sheep, then brought the sheep to her, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, and the sheep had given birth. He (peace be upon him) said: If the sheep were pregnant with him, he returns half of the sheep and half of their offspring; and if the pregnancy was not with him, he returns half of the sheep and does not return anything from the offspring.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Similar to it, except that he said: He brought to her sheep and slaves, so the sheep and the slaves gave birth.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage (entered with her)
key_terms.رَقِيقاً: Slaves (male or female, as a form of wealth/dower)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning half the dowry if it consists of livestock that gave birth before divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence regarding the division of dower (mahr) when it consists of livestock and the couple is divorced before consummation, distinguishing between offspring born during the husband's possession versus those born after separation. It reflects the practical application of Quranic principles by Imam al-Sadiq, emphasizing fairness in asset division based on actual ownership duration. The ruling highlights the importance of determining whether the 'fruit' (offspring) accrued while the principal asset was under the husband's control, a key concept in Islamic inheritance and property law.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man who married a woman upon one hundred sheep, then ushers the sheep to her. Then he divorces her before sleeping with her, and the sheep have given birth’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the sheep were impregnated when they were with him, half of these would be returned with half of the children; and they were not impregnated when they were with him, half of these (sheep) would be returned and nothing from the children would be returned’.
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it except that he said, ‘He ushered to her sheep and a slave. So the sheep and the slave gave birth’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman and sets a mahr (dower) of one hundred sheep. He then delivers them to her, then divorces her before going to bed with her and the sheep have given birth to their young. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the sheep had become pregnant with him she must return one-half of them and one-half of the young ones; but if they did not become pregnant with him she must return one-half of the sheep but not the young ones. 555

Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has narrated the following: “He has narrated a similar Hadith from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, except that he has said, ‘He delivered sheep and slaves, then sheep and slaves gave birth. 555
